subject.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args

question: Should OpenClaw advertise `model`, `fallbacks`, `toolsAllow`, and `timeoutSeconds` as flat model-facing cron add/update fields while rejecting shell/on-exit fields and leaving `contextTokens`/`maxSpendUsd` to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/64721?
rationale: The implementation follows existing cron runtime fields, but exposing provider selection and tool allow-list controls to model-generated scheduled turns is a product and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Accept the narrow flat repair
options.body: Land this PR as the supported flat schema for model, fallbacks, toolsAllow, and timeoutSeconds, and keep contextTokens/maxSpendUsd separate in the linked issue.

options.title: Narrow the flat surface
options.body: Ask the PR to advertise only schedule and message fields, leaving model routing and tool access overrides to a separate maintainer decision.

options.title: Pause for the wider cron contract
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers decide the full scheduled agent-turn control contract, including the remaining context and spend fields.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow flat repair
recommendation.body: Land this PR as the supported flat schema for model, fallbacks, toolsAllow, and timeoutSeconds, and keep contextTokens/maxSpendUsd separate in the linked issue.

likelyOwner.reason: mmaps has the strongest merged history on scheduled-turn tool policy, which is the most sensitive open choice in this PR.
